data.objective: Observe major geopolitical, political, diplomatic, and China-related developments and identify meaningful events or changes happening today.
data.initialContextTokenization: Estimated with the local gpt-4o tokenizer; foundational context only.

indicator.name: S&P 500
indicator.description: A market-capitalization-weighted index of 500 leading publicly traded U.S. companies across major industries, representing a broad measure of the large-cap U.S. equity market. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor broad U.S. equity-market performance and assess changes in investor risk appetite, financial conditions, market expectations, and the valuation of large-cap U.S. companies.
indicator.purpose: Provide a broad benchmark for U.S. large-cap equity markets for analyzing financial-market conditions, risk sentiment, economic expectations, and relationships between equity markets and macroeconomic indicators.
indicator.significance: The S&P 500 is a widely followed benchmark for the U.S. large-cap equity market. Changes in the index provide information about equity-market performance and investor expectations and can help contextualize broader financial conditions and risk sentiment. The series is a price index and does not include dividends or represent total return.

indicator.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicator.description: A market-capitalization-weighted index tracking more than 3,000 common equities listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market, including common stocks, American depositary receipts, real estate investment trusts, and tracking stocks. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor broad U.S. equity-market performance across companies listed on the NASDAQ and assess changes in market sentiment, risk appetite, and the performance of growth-oriented and technology-heavy segments of the equity market.
indicator.purpose: Provide a broad benchmark for NASDAQ-listed equities for analyzing equity-market conditions, investor risk appetite, market expectations, and changes across technology and growth-oriented portions of the U.S. stock market.
indicator.significance: The NASDAQ Composite provides broad exposure to equities listed on the NASDAQ Stock Market and includes companies across multiple industries, with substantial representation from technology and growth-oriented businesses. Changes in the index provide information about equity-market performance and investor expectations and can help contextualize broader financial-market conditions.

indicator.name: Dow Jones Industrial Average
indicator.description: A stock-market index tracking 30 large, established U.S. companies across a range of industries. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor the performance of a group of large U.S. companies and assess changes in equity-market conditions, investor sentiment, risk appetite, and market expectations.
indicator.purpose: Provide a widely followed benchmark for large-cap U.S. equities for analyzing financial-market conditions, equity performance, investor risk appetite, and changes in market expectations.
indicator.significance: The Dow Jones Industrial Average provides a market-based measure of the performance of 30 large U.S. companies across multiple industries. Changes in the index provide information about equity-market performance and can help contextualize broader financial conditions and investor sentiment.

indicator.name: Russell 2000 Index
indicator.description: A daily measure of the Russell 2000 Index, a benchmark for U.S. small-cap equities, reported through Financial Modeling Prep. The indicator provides daily open, close, absolute change, and percentage change for the index.
indicator.use: Track daily movements in the Russell 2000 Index, including opening level, closing level, absolute price change, and percentage change, to monitor U.S. small-cap equity-market conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide visibility into the performance and short-term direction of U.S. small-cap equities as a distinct segment of the broader U.S. stock market.
indicator.significance: The Russell 2000 is a widely used benchmark for U.S. small-cap equities and provides a different market perspective from large-cap indexes such as the S&P 500 and technology-heavy indexes such as the Nasdaq-100. Movements in the index can provide context for investor risk appetite, domestic economic expectations, financial conditions, credit conditions, and the relative performance of smaller U.S. companies. Because smaller companies can be more sensitive to domestic economic activity and financing conditions, Russell 2000 performance can complement broader equity-market indicators when analyzing U.S. market conditions and risk sentiment.

indicator.name: CBOE Volatility Index
indicator.description: A market-based measure of expected near-term volatility in U.S. stock markets derived from stock index option prices. The series is reported as a daily closing index value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in market-implied expectations for near-term equity-market volatility and identify shifts in financial-market uncertainty and risk conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of expected near-term stock-market volatility for analyzing investor risk expectations, market stress, financial conditions, and changes in market sentiment.
indicator.significance: The VIX reflects volatility expectations implied by stock index option prices. Changes in the index provide information about shifts in expected near-term equity-market volatility and can help contextualize changes in broader financial-market risk conditions.

indicator.name: Nominal Broad U.S. Dollar Index
indicator.description: A trade-weighted index measuring the value of the U.S. dollar against a broad group of foreign currencies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in the broad nominal value of the U.S. dollar and assess foreign-exchange conditions, international financial conditions, trade competitiveness, and cross-border capital flows.
indicator.purpose: Provide a broad measure of U.S. dollar strength against major trading-partner currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, monetary policy transmission, global financial conditions, and relationships between the dollar and other asset markets.
indicator.significance: The broad U.S. dollar index provides a trade-weighted measure of changes in the dollar's value across a broad set of foreign currencies. Changes in the index can affect import prices, export competitiveness, international capital flows, commodity pricing, and global financial conditions.

indicator.name: Nominal Advanced Foreign Economies U.S. Dollar Index
indicator.description: A trade-weighted index measuring the nominal value of the U.S. dollar against currencies of advanced foreign economies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in the U.S. dollar's nominal value against currencies of advanced foreign economies and assess exchange-rate conditions, international financial conditions, and cross-border economic relationships.
indicator.purpose: Provide a trade-weighted measure of the U.S. dollar against advanced-economy currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, relative currency movements, monetary policy transmission, and international financial conditions.
indicator.significance: The index isolates movements in the U.S. dollar relative to currencies of advanced foreign economies using trade-weighted exchange rates. Changes can provide information about dollar strength, international capital conditions, trade relationships, and differences in monetary and economic conditions across major advanced economies.

indicator.name: Nominal Emerging Market Economies U.S. Dollar Index
indicator.description: A trade-weighted index measuring the nominal value of the U.S. dollar against currencies of emerging market economies. The index is reported daily, is not seasonally adjusted, and uses January 2006 = 100 as its reference period.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in the U.S. dollar's nominal value against currencies of emerging market economies and assess foreign-exchange conditions, global financial conditions, capital flows, and international economic relationships.
indicator.purpose: Provide a trade-weighted measure of the U.S. dollar against emerging-market currencies for analyzing foreign-exchange conditions, international financial conditions, monetary policy transmission, and changes in cross-border capital flows.
indicator.significance: The index measures movements in the U.S. dollar relative to currencies of emerging market economies using trade-weighted exchange rates. Changes in the index can provide information about dollar strength, emerging-market financial conditions, international capital flows, and differences in monetary and economic conditions across emerging markets.

indicator.name: EUR/USD
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the euro and the U.S. dollar, representing the value of one euro in U.S. dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor EUR/USD movements and assess changes in euro-area and U.S. monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, relative economic conditions, capital flows, trade conditions, and global market sentiment.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the euro and U.S. dollar for analyzing relative currency strength, ECB and Federal Reserve policy expectations, euro-area and U.S. interest-rate differentials, cross-border capital flows, and changes in global financial conditions.
indicator.significance: EUR/USD is one of the world's most important foreign-exchange pairs, linking the euro area with the United States and their respective monetary systems. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in ECB and Federal Reserve policy expectations, relative economic growth and inflation, interest rates, international capital flows, trade conditions, and global risk sentiment. EUR/USD movements also influence euro-area import prices, inflation, and financial conditions.

indicator.name: GBP/USD
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the British pound sterling and the U.S. dollar, representing the value of one British pound in U.S. dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor GBP/USD movements and assess changes in UK-U.S. monetary policy expectations, currency strength, interest-rate differentials, and broader global financial conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the British pound and U.S. dollar for analyzing relative currency strength, UK-U.S. interest-rate differentials, monetary policy expectations, and cross-border financial conditions.
indicator.significance: GBP/USD is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United Kingdom and United States. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in relative economic conditions, monetary policy expectations, interest rates, capital flows, and market risk sentiment.

indicator.name: USD/JPY
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen, representing the value of one U.S. dollar in Japanese yen. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor USD/JPY movements and assess changes in U.S.-Japan monetary policy expectations, currency strength, interest-rate differentials, and broader global financial conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Japanese yen for analyzing relative currency strength, U.S.-Japan interest-rate differentials, monetary policy expectations, and cross-border financial conditions.
indicator.significance: USD/JPY is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United States and Japan. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in relative economic conditions, Federal Reserve and Bank of Japan policy expectations, interest rates, capital flows, and global risk sentiment.

indicator.name: USD/CAD
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Canadian dollar, representing the value of one U.S. dollar in Canadian dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor USD/CAD movements and assess changes in U.S.-Canadian monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, Canadian dollar strength, commodity prices, energy markets, and North American financial conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the exchange rate between the U.S. dollar and Canadian dollar for analyzing relative currency strength, U.S.-Canadian interest-rate differentials, commodity-driven economic conditions, and changes in cross-border financial markets.
indicator.significance: USD/CAD is a major foreign-exchange pair linking the United States and Canada. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in Federal Reserve and Bank of Canada policy expectations, interest rates, Canadian commodity prices and export conditions, particularly energy, trade flows, and broader North American economic and market conditions.

indicator.name: AUD/USD
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the Australian dollar and the U.S. dollar, representing the value of one Australian dollar in U.S. dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor AUD/USD movements and assess changes in Australian-U.S. monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, commodity prices, terms of trade, China-linked economic conditions, and global risk sentiment.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the Australian dollar against the U.S. dollar for analyzing Australian currency strength, Australia-U.S. interest-rate differentials, commodity-driven trade conditions, and changes in global market risk appetite.
indicator.significance: AUD/USD is a major foreign-exchange pair connecting Australia and the United States and is closely associated with Australia's commodity-export economy. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in relative monetary policy expectations and interest rates, commodity prices and Australia's terms of trade, Chinese economic conditions, capital flows, and global risk sentiment.

indicator.name: NZD/USD
indicator.description: The daily exchange rate between the New Zealand dollar and the U.S. dollar, representing the value of one New Zealand dollar in U.S. dollars. The series provides daily open, high, low, and closing exchange rates.
indicator.use: Monitor NZD/USD movements and assess changes in New Zealand-U.S. monetary policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, currency strength, commodity and export conditions, Asia-Pacific economic activity, and global risk sentiment.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the New Zealand dollar against the U.S. dollar for analyzing New Zealand currency strength, New Zealand-U.S. interest-rate differentials, trade and export conditions, and changes in global market risk appetite.
indicator.significance: NZD/USD is a major foreign-exchange pair linking New Zealand and the United States. Changes in the exchange rate can reflect shifts in Reserve Bank of New Zealand and Federal Reserve policy expectations, interest rates, New Zealand's terms of trade and export prices, economic conditions in China and the Asia-Pacific region, capital flows, and global risk sentiment.

indicator.name: Federal Funds Rate
indicator.description: The effective interest rate at which U.S. depository institutions lend federal funds to one another overnight. It is a market-determined rate influenced by the Federal Reserve's monetary policy framework and target range.
indicator.use: Monitor the stance and transmission of U.S. monetary policy and assess changes in short-term interest rates, liquidity, financial conditions, and broader economic activity.
indicator.purpose: Provide a core measure of short-term U.S. interest rates for monetary policy analysis, financial condition analysis, and cross-indicator interpretation within the intelligence system.
indicator.significance: The federal funds rate is a central short-term interest rate in the U.S. financial system. Changes in the rate influence other short-term rates and indirectly affect borrowing costs, financial conditions, economic activity, and asset markets.

indicator.name: 2-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on U.S. Treasury securities with a constant maturity of two years, quoted on an investment basis. It reflects market expectations and pricing for short-term U.S. government borrowing.
indicator.use: Monitor short-term U.S. interest rates, Treasury market conditions, monetary policy expectations, and changes in the cost of government borrowing.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the two-year point on the U.S. Treasury yield curve for analyzing interest-rate expectations, monetary policy, financial conditions, and relationships across the yield curve.
indicator.significance: The two-year Treasury yield is closely connected to expectations for future monetary policy and short-term interest rates. Changes in the yield can provide information about shifts in interest-rate expectations and broader financial conditions.

indicator.name: 5-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on U.S. Treasury securities with a constant maturity of five years, quoted on an investment basis. The series is reported daily and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor intermediate-term U.S. Treasury interest rates and assess changes in market expectations, monetary policy transmission, inflation expectations, and broader financial conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the five-year point on the U.S. Treasury yield curve for analyzing intermediate-term interest rates, economic expectations, monetary policy, and changes in financial conditions.
indicator.significance: The five-year Treasury yield reflects market pricing for intermediate-term U.S. government borrowing and incorporates expectations about future interest rates, inflation, and economic conditions. Changes in the yield can provide information about shifts in the middle portion of the Treasury yield curve and broader financial-market expectations.

indicator.name: 10-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on U.S. Treasury securities with a constant maturity of ten years, quoted on an investment basis. It reflects market pricing for longer-term U.S. government borrowing and expectations about future economic and financial conditions.
indicator.use: Monitor long-term U.S. interest rates, Treasury market conditions, financial conditions, inflation and growth expectations, and changes in the cost of government borrowing.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the ten-year point on the U.S. Treasury yield curve for analyzing long-term interest rates, economic expectations, monetary policy transmission, and financial market conditions.
indicator.significance: The 10-year Treasury yield is a major benchmark for U.S. long-term interest rates and influences pricing across financial markets. Changes in the yield can reflect shifts in expectations for inflation, economic growth, monetary policy, and demand for government securities.

indicator.name: Real 10-Year Treasury Yield
indicator.description: The market yield on 10-year U.S. Treasury securities whose principal and interest payments are adjusted for inflation. It represents a market-based measure of the real interest rate for a 10-year maturity.
indicator.use: Monitor real long-term interest rates and assess changes in inflation-adjusted borrowing costs, financial conditions, and market expectations.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of the real 10-year U.S. interest rate for analyzing real borrowing costs, inflation-adjusted returns, monetary policy, and financial conditions.
indicator.significance: The real 10-year Treasury yield provides information about the inflation-adjusted cost of long-term capital and the pricing of inflation-indexed government securities. Changes in the yield can affect financial conditions and the relative attractiveness of real versus nominal assets.

indicator.name: High Yield Credit Spread
indicator.description: The ICE BofA U.S. High Yield Index Option-Adjusted Spread, measuring the spread between below-investment-grade U.S. corporate bonds and a comparable Treasury yield curve after adjusting for embedded options. The series is reported as a daily closing value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor credit-market conditions and changes in the compensation investors demand for holding below-investment-grade corporate debt relative to U.S. Treasury securities.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of high-yield corporate credit spreads for analyzing credit risk, financial conditions, investor risk pricing, and changes in stress across corporate bond markets.
indicator.significance: The high-yield credit spread reflects the additional yield demanded by investors for below-investment-grade corporate debt relative to a Treasury reference curve. Changes in the spread can provide information about shifts in perceived credit risk, risk appetite, and broader financial-market conditions.

indicator.name: Investment Grade Credit Spread
indicator.description: The ICE BofA U.S. Corporate Index Option-Adjusted Spread, measuring the spread between investment-grade U.S. corporate bonds and a comparable Treasury yield curve after adjusting for embedded options. The series is reported as a daily closing value and is not seasonally adjusted.
indicator.use: Monitor credit-market conditions and changes in the compensation investors demand for holding investment-grade corporate debt relative to U.S. Treasury securities.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-based measure of investment-grade corporate credit spreads for analyzing credit risk, financial conditions, investor risk pricing, and changes in corporate bond markets.
indicator.significance: The investment-grade credit spread reflects the additional yield demanded by investors for investment-grade corporate debt relative to a Treasury reference curve. Changes in the spread can provide information about shifts in perceived credit risk, risk appetite, and broader financial-market conditions.

indicator.name: CNN Fear & Greed Index
indicator.description: A daily composite index designed by CNN to measure prevailing fear and greed in the U.S. stock market using multiple market-behavior indicators. The index ranges from 0 to 100, with lower values representing greater fear and higher values representing greater greed.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in U.S. equity-market sentiment, investor risk appetite, market momentum, volatility, and demand for defensive assets, and identify shifts between risk-seeking and risk-averse market conditions.
indicator.purpose: Provide a compact market-sentiment signal that summarizes several observable characteristics of U.S. equity markets into a single daily measure for tracking changes in investor risk appetite and market stress.
indicator.significance: The Fear & Greed Index provides a behavioral measure of the prevailing emotional conditions in U.S. equity markets. Changes in the index can indicate shifts in market momentum, volatility, demand for safe-haven assets, and willingness to take risk. It can therefore provide context for interpreting market moves alongside prices, volatility measures, credit conditions, and broader financial-market indicators.

indicator.name: CNN Market Volatility (VIX vs 50-Day Moving Average)
indicator.description: A daily market-volatility indicator based on the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX) relative to its 50-day moving average. The VIX reflects expected S&P 500 volatility over the following 30 days, while its relationship with the 50-day average is used by CNN as a measure of changing market volatility and fear.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in expected U.S. equity-market volatility and identify shifts in market stress, risk aversion, and investor sentiment through the VIX's relationship with its 50-day trend.
indicator.purpose: Provide a volatility-based measure of U.S. equity-market conditions that captures whether expected market volatility is increasing or decreasing relative to its recent trend.
indicator.significance: The VIX provides a forward-looking measure of expected S&P 500 volatility derived from options prices. Comparing it with its 50-day moving average adds a trend dimension that helps identify changes in market stress and risk perception. Rising volatility relative to its trend is interpreted by CNN as a signal of fear, while declining volatility is associated with greed. As one component of the Fear & Greed framework, it complements momentum, breadth, options positioning, and other measures of market behavior.

indicator.name: CNN Safe Haven Demand
indicator.description: A daily measure of the difference between U.S. Treasury bond and stock returns over the previous 20 trading days. It is used by CNN to assess whether investors are favoring safer Treasury assets over riskier equities.
indicator.use: Monitor shifts between equity risk-taking and demand for safer Treasury assets, and identify changes in investor risk appetite, defensive positioning, and market stress.
indicator.purpose: Provide a cross-asset measure of investor risk preference by comparing recent stock and Treasury performance over a 20-trading-day period.
indicator.significance: Safe Haven Demand captures changes in investor preference between riskier equities and safer Treasury assets. When Treasury bonds outperform stocks, it can indicate increased demand for defensive assets and greater risk aversion; when stocks outperform Treasuries, it indicates stronger relative demand for risk assets. As a component of CNN's Fear & Greed framework, it adds a cross-asset risk-preference signal that complements equity momentum, breadth, volatility, and options positioning.

indicator.name: CNN Put/Call Options
indicator.description: A daily put-to-call options ratio used by CNN as a measure of U.S. equity-market sentiment. The ratio compares put-option activity with call-option activity and is translated into a Fear & Greed rating.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in equity-options positioning and assess shifts in investor risk appetite, hedging activity, speculative demand, and market sentiment within the CNN Fear & Greed framework.
indicator.purpose: Provide an options-market sentiment measure that captures changes in the relative demand for put and call options and adds information about investor positioning and perceived market risk to broader market-health analysis.
indicator.significance: The put/call ratio provides information about how options-market activity is distributed between puts and calls. Relatively greater put activity can reflect increased demand for downside protection or bearish positioning, while relatively greater call activity can reflect greater demand for upside exposure or speculative positioning. As a component of CNN's Fear & Greed Index, the ratio provides a market-positioning signal that complements momentum, breadth, volatility, and other measures of investor behavior.

indicator.name: CNN Stock Price Breadth
indicator.description: A daily CNN market-breadth indicator measuring the breadth of stock-price performance across the U.S. equity market and translating the result into a Fear & Greed rating.
indicator.use: Monitor how broadly stock-price gains or declines are distributed across the U.S. equity market and identify changes in market participation, breadth, and overall equity-market strength.
indicator.purpose: Provide a market-health measure of equity-market breadth that helps determine whether prevailing stock-market conditions are supported by broad participation across stocks or concentrated in a narrower portion of the market.
indicator.significance: Stock-price breadth provides information about the participation underlying movements in the U.S. equity market. Strong breadth indicates that price strength is distributed across a larger portion of the market, while weak breadth indicates narrower participation or broader selling pressure. As a component of CNN's Fear & Greed framework, the indicator adds a market-participation dimension that complements price momentum, volatility, options activity, and other measures of investor behavior.

indicator.name: AAII Investor Sentiment Survey
indicator.description: A weekly survey of individual investors measuring the percentage who expect the U.S. stock market to rise, remain essentially unchanged, or fall over the next six months. The dataset includes bullish, neutral, bearish, and bull-bear spread readings.
indicator.use: Monitor changes in individual-investor expectations, optimism, pessimism, uncertainty, and overall sentiment toward the U.S. stock market, including changes in the bull-bear spread.
indicator.purpose: Provide a direct survey-based measure of individual-investor expectations that complements market-derived sentiment indicators by capturing what retail investors expect the stock market to do over the following six months.
indicator.significance: The AAII Sentiment Survey provides a direct measure of individual-investor expectations rather than inferring sentiment from market prices or positioning. Changes in bullish, neutral, and bearish responses reveal shifts in optimism, pessimism, and uncertainty, while the bull-bear spread summarizes the balance between optimistic and pessimistic views. Extreme sentiment readings can provide useful context for assessing investor psychology and potential sentiment reversals, but the survey does not establish the future direction of the market.

indicator.name: IG WTI Crude Oil Retail Positioning
indicator.description: A daily measure of long and short positioning among retail traders on the IG trading platform for WTI crude oil. The indicator reports the percentage of IG retail traders holding long and short positions and the resulting net positioning. This data represents IG's own retail trader pool and is not a market-wide measure of all retail traders or investors.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in long and short positioning among IG retail traders exposed to WTI crude oil, including the distribution of positions and the resulting net retail positioning.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of how IG's retail trader population is positioned toward WTI crude oil and how that positioning changes over time.
indicator.significance: IG WTI crude oil retail positioning provides a daily view of directional exposure among retail traders using the IG trading platform. The indicator can provide context for retail sentiment, speculative positioning, and changes in exposure to the crude oil market. Because the dataset represents only IG's retail trader pool rather than the entire retail-investor population, it should be interpreted as a broker-specific positioning signal rather than a comprehensive measure of overall retail sentiment. WTI positioning can be analyzed alongside crude oil supply and demand, OPEC policy, oil inventories, global economic growth, inflation, the U.S. dollar, interest rates, and the Brent-WTI relationship to provide additional context for energy-market conditions.

indicator.name: IG Brent Crude Oil Retail Positioning
indicator.description: A daily measure of long and short positioning among retail traders on the IG trading platform for Brent crude oil. The indicator reports the percentage of IG retail traders holding long and short positions and the resulting net positioning. This data represents IG's own retail trader pool and is not a market-wide measure of all retail traders or investors.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in long and short positioning among IG retail traders exposed to Brent crude oil, including the distribution of positions and the resulting net retail positioning.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of how IG's retail trader population is positioned toward Brent crude oil and how that positioning changes over time.
indicator.significance: IG Brent crude oil retail positioning provides a daily view of directional exposure among retail traders using the IG trading platform. The indicator can provide context for retail sentiment, speculative positioning, and changes in exposure to the global crude oil market. Because the dataset represents only IG's retail trader pool rather than the entire retail-investor population, it should be interpreted as a broker-specific positioning signal rather than a comprehensive measure of overall retail sentiment. Brent positioning can be analyzed alongside crude oil supply and demand, OPEC policy, oil inventories, geopolitical developments, global economic growth, the U.S. dollar, and the Brent-WTI relationship to provide additional context for global energy-market conditions.

indicator.name: IG Gold Retail Positioning
indicator.description: A daily measure of long and short positioning among retail traders on the IG trading platform for gold. The indicator reports the percentage of IG retail traders holding long and short positions and the resulting net positioning. This data represents IG's own retail trader pool and is not a market-wide measure of all retail traders or investors.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in long and short positioning among IG retail traders exposed to gold, including the distribution of positions and the resulting net retail positioning.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of how IG's retail trader population is positioned toward gold and how that positioning changes over time.
indicator.significance: IG gold retail positioning provides a daily view of directional exposure among retail traders using the IG trading platform. The indicator can provide context for retail sentiment, speculative positioning, and changes in exposure to gold. Because the dataset represents only IG's retail trader pool rather than the entire retail-investor population, it should be interpreted as a broker-specific positioning signal rather than a comprehensive measure of overall retail sentiment. Gold positioning can be analyzed alongside gold prices, safe-haven demand, inflation expectations, real interest rates, Treasury yields, the U.S. dollar, Federal Reserve policy, and broader financial-market conditions to provide additional context for changes in gold-market positioning.

indicator.name: IG Silver Retail Positioning
indicator.description: A daily measure of long and short positioning among retail traders on the IG trading platform for silver. The indicator reports the percentage of IG retail traders holding long and short positions and the resulting net positioning. This data represents IG's own retail trader pool and is not a market-wide measure of all retail traders or investors.
indicator.use: Track daily changes in long and short positioning among IG retail traders exposed to silver, including the distribution of positions and the resulting net retail positioning.
indicator.purpose: Provide a daily view of how IG's retail trader population is positioned toward silver and how that positioning changes over time.
indicator.significance: IG silver retail positioning provides a daily view of directional exposure among retail traders using the IG trading platform. The indicator can provide context for retail sentiment, speculative positioning, and changes in exposure to silver. Because the dataset represents only IG's retail trader pool rather than the entire retail-investor population, it should be interpreted as a broker-specific positioning signal rather than a comprehensive measure of overall retail sentiment. Silver positioning can be analyzed alongside silver prices, gold, industrial demand, manufacturing activity, inflation expectations, real interest rates, Treasury yields, the U.S. dollar, Federal Reserve policy, and broader risk sentiment to provide additional context for precious-metals and industrial-demand conditions.

indicator.name: CFTC U.S. Dollar Index Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of U.S. Dollar Index futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates U.S. Dollar Index futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Funds, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable.
indicator.use: Track changes in U.S. Dollar Index futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including changes in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in U.S. Dollar Index futures and how their exposure to broad U.S. dollar strength changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC U.S. Dollar Index futures positioning provides a structured view of market-participant exposure to the U.S. dollar relative to a basket of major foreign currencies. Changes in open interest reveal changes in futures-market participation, while changes in long and short positions show how different trader groups are adjusting dollar exposure. Dollar positioning can provide context for broad USD strength, global foreign-exchange conditions, U.S. monetary-policy expectations, interest-rate differentials, commodity prices, international financial conditions, and global risk sentiment.

indicator.name: CFTC Euro FX Futures Positioning
indicator.description: A weekly measure of Euro FX futures open interest and trader positioning reported by the CFTC's Traders in Financial Futures report. The data separates Euro FX futures positions into Dealer/Intermediary, Asset Manager/Institutional, Leveraged Funds, Other Reportables, and Nonreportables, with long, short, spreading, and net exposure measures where applicable.
indicator.use: Track changes in Euro FX futures open interest and positioning across dealers, asset managers, leveraged funds, other reportable traders, and nonreportable traders, including changes in long, short, spreading, and net exposure.
indicator.purpose: Provide asset-specific visibility into how different classes of market participants are positioned in Euro FX futures and how their exposure to the euro changes over time.
indicator.significance: CFTC Euro FX futures positioning provides a structured view of market-participant exposure to the euro through regulated currency futures. results.title: Trump insists energy ceasefire holds as Ukraine reports new Russian strikes | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
highlights: Trump insists energy ceasefire holds as Ukraine reports new Russian strikes | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera Trump insists energy ceasefire holds as Ukraine reports new Russian strikes US president urges Zelenskyy, Putin to end ‘ridiculous war’ and insists the two nations have agreed to stop attacks on energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy urges pressure on Russia as NATO warns against escalation United States President Donald Trump has insisted that Russia and Ukraine have agreed to stop striking each other’s energy infrastructure, as he called on both sides to end the “ridiculous” war. Trump’s comments on Monday came even as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russian forces had struck at least six Ukrainian energy facilities since the US president declared the truce on Sunday. The US president called the war, which began with Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, a “disaster” and claimed, without offering evidence, that at least 32,000 people had been killed this month alone. “All I know is that Zelenskyy and Putin have to get together and end that ridiculous war,” he said. Trump had blindsided Kyiv and its European allies when he announced the purported energy ceasefire on Sunday. The announcement came two days after he temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian diesel, a move that drew outrage in Europe and Ukraine. Zelenskyy said on Monday that Ukraine supported an energy ceasefire and had carried out no attacks on Russian refineries overnight. He said Kyiv was prepared to sign “guarantees to make sure they can be trusted”. But he said it was “increasingly evident” that Moscow would not comply. “Today alone, the Russians have attacked 6 energy facilities in Ukraine. 33 people were wounded across the country,” Zelenskyy wrote on social media. “This is what happens when Russia sees the prospect of higher revenues for its war machine.” Russia, however, has rejected any pause in fighting, with Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov promising to press ahead with the military campaign. “I do not think he deserves a respite,” he said of Zelenskyy. “I don’t think we’ll be buying into assurances and promises again.” Russia, he added, would continue to pursue the goals of what it calls its “special military operation” in Ukraine. Trump, meanwhile, has portrayed Ukraine, rather than Russia, as the main obstacle to peace. He has said that Putin is more eager on a deal than Zelenskyy, and has called on Ukrainians to vote their president out of office – an unusually harsh turn in a relationship that has been strained since Trump returned to the White House in 2025. The latest announcement, according to our correspondent, appeared to be driven by Trump’s desire to bring down diesel prices before the US midterm elections on November 3. Ukraine’s European allies, meanwhile, voiced scepticism about the energy ceasefire and approved the largest set of European Union sanctions since Russia’s 2022 invasion. The bloc’s foreign ministers added some 1,569 people and businesses to the bloc’s sanctions list to maintain the pressure on Moscow. “Russia will only negotiate seriously under pressure, which is why we are sticking to our sanctions against Russia,” German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said in Berlin.

Defense Intelligence's War and Sanctions portal. The crude oil tanker is sanctioned by the U.S, EU, Switzerland, Canada, and Japan. Two cargo ships were struck by drones near Bulgaria's Black Sea coast overnight on Oct. 13, Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev said. Radev said there was no clear and conclusive evidence to attribute responsibility to either the Ukrainian or Russian side, but argued that "the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation." The group included two women, a child, and several men who were being led toward the Shebelinka–Ostrogozhsk gas pipeline, according to Ukraine's 13th Khartia Corps. The group came under repeated mortar and artillery fire as it moved. Drone footage recorded by Ukrainian reconnaissance units showed casualties among the civilians, Khartia said, adding that Ukrainian troops had not opened fire. Based on the impact patterns, the strike originated from the eastern bank of the Oskil River, where Russian forces are positioned, the corps said. The military said it was still establishing the number of casualties. `Russian drone strikes university building in Rivne, injures 25` A Russian drone struck a university building in the northwestern city of Rivne, injuring 25 people, Rivne's National Police branch said on Oct. 13. Ukraine's Education and Science Minister Andrii Butenko said that a fire broke out in a building of Rivne State Humanitarian University as a result of the Russian drone strike. The Faculty of Music building was almost completely gutted by the fire, while neighboring teaching facilities had windows smashed, he added. Oleksandr Koval, head of Rivne Oblast Military Administration, said on Oct. 13 that the drone strike damaged the second floor of the building. The fire in the building had been contained, and emergency services were on site. At around 10:35 a.m., Ukraine's air force had reported a jet-powered drone flying over Rivne. results.title: EU cautious over Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ as Russia continues Ukraine attacks - RFI
highlights: EU cautious over Trump’s ‘energy ceasefire’ as Russia continues Ukraine attacks - RFI The European Union has given a cautious welcome to the prospect of an “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, as winter approaches and renewed Russian strikes put fresh pressure on the country’s power network. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas struck a cautious note on Monday, saying Brussels wanted to see clear evidence that Moscow intended to respect the proposed halt to attacks on energy infrastructure announced by US President Donald Trump. “We welcome the energy ceasefire when it holds,” Kallas told reporters ahead of a meeting of EU foreign ministers. “We haven’t yet seen that also Russia will stick to it.” Those doubts deepened through the day as Ukraine said Russia had continued to strike energy sites, while the Kremlin stopped short of confirming that any ceasefire had been agreed. The dispute comes amid wider unease among Ukraine’s European allies after Trump announced at the weekend a temporary easing of US sanctions on Russian diesel – a move Kyiv and several European governments fear could reduce pressure on President Vladimir Putin to end the war. Trump defended the diesel deal on Monday despite criticism from US lawmakers in both parties. He also insisted Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an energy ceasefire, telling reporters: “They agreed because I said they agreed.” Trump sowed confusion on Sunday when he announced an “ energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine without setting out its terms or explaining how it would be enforced. But Russia continued attacking Ukraine’s power infrastructure. Russia said contacts were continuing over a possible energy ceasefire, but Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov rejected Kyiv’s call for a broader pause. “We do not want a ceasefire,” he said. “We want long-term peace and are prepared to do everything possible to achieve it.” With colder weather approaching, attacks on the electricity network remain a central concern after successive winters in which Russia has targeted Ukrainian energy infrastructure. Kallas warned that any agreement would also need to go beyond oil refineries, arguing that a narrowly defined truce would favour Moscow because Russia has far greater refining capacity. “If we want to end this war, the only way we can do this is putting more pressure on Russia,” she said, urging Washington to increase rather than ease sanctions. The offer fell well short of Kyiv’s call for the security conditions needed to organise voting while millions of Ukrainians remain displaced at home and abroad. Lithuanian Prime Minister Mindaugas Sinkevicius told the forum that Ukraine’s allies should encourage Kyiv to strike more Russian data centres as part of efforts to counter Moscow’s hybrid warfare capabilities. results.title: Russia pounds Ukrainian cities, spares energy targets for first time since Trump 'ceasefire' - France 24
highlights: Russia pounds Ukrainian cities, spares energy targets for first time since Trump 'ceasefire' - France 24 Russia hammered Ukrainian cities and transport links overnight into Tuesday, killing at least four people in the city of Kharkiv, while appearing to spare energy facilities for the first time since US President Donald Trump announced an "energy ceasefire" at the weekend. It was not clear whether Moscow had deliberately avoided targeting power plants. Russia hit no Ukrainian energy targets on Tuesday for the first time since US President Donald Trump's weekend announcement of an "energy ceasefire", while hammering cities' transport and logistics overnight with ballistic missiles and drones. Russia's defence ministry, in its daily summary of overnight strikes, made no mention of Ukrainian energy facilities. A Kremlin spokesman, asked about the energy ceasefire, would only say that contacts were ongoing, but declined to provide any further details. However, one missile came down just over a kilometre from a plant providing heating to much of the city of Lviv, in the west. Trump's ceasefire announcement on Sunday came two days after his declaration of a deal that lifted US sanctions on Russian diesel exports to allow Russia to supply almost 2 million metric tons of diesel, a bid to lower US fuel prices. Reuters and other media outlets have reported that US officials have threatened to cut off intelligence sharing and weapons sales to Ukraine unless it halts its strikes on Russian oil refineries. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Tuesday that Ukraine had not hit Russian refineries for two days, since Trump announced the ceasefire, but that Russia had continued attacks on energy and critical infrastructure during that time. Russia struck six Ukrainian energy sites on Monday. It was not clear whether Russia had deliberately avoided targeting energy infrastructure overnight into Tuesday. Trump has repeatedly blamed Ukrainian attacks – which prompted Moscow to suspend diesel exports – for a sharp rise in US diesel prices this year, a headache for his Republican party ahead of Congressional midterm elections in three weeks. Most analysts, however, say Trump's war in Iran has had a far greater impact on the price rise. Four people were killed by Russian strikes in Ukraine's second city, Kharkiv, and at least a dozen were injured across the country, Ukrainian officials said. The Ukrainian air force said it had not received prior surveillance warnings before Russia fired six ballistic missiles at Kyiv late Monday, prompting widespread anxiety in online comments from residents. "The causes are being investigated," it said in a statement. Intelligence about preparations for ballistic missile attacks has been part of the information that the US provides to Ukraine, Ukrainian officials say. Zelensky's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Tuesday that Kyiv continues to receive intelligence data from the United States. Speaking at a Warsaw security conference, Sybiha said the US request to halt attacks on Russian refineries showed how Ukraine's position had strengthened, alluding to Trump's comment to Zelenskiy in a tense Oval Office meeting last year that "you don't have the cards". "In less than two years, we have gone playing your cards That is an achievement," Sybiha said. Zelensky has said Ukraine supports the idea of an energy truce, but he has accused Moscow of violating the ceasefire – which Moscow has not acknowledged signing up to. "This winter, if Russia does not agree to an energy ceasefire, we will respond," Zelensky told a security conference in Warsaw on Monday. The Ukrainian air force said on Tuesday that damage had been recorded at 17 locations overnight. Air defence units downed 88 out of 108 Russian drones, it said. A cargo terminal in the southern Mykolaiv region and transport infrastructure in the southeastern Dnipropetrovsk region were damaged. In Kharkiv, four people were killed and at least 11 injured in a residential building. In the western Khmelnytskyi region, a hospital was damaged, regional officials said.

results.title: Germany To Start Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities'
highlights: Germany To Start Nord Stream 'War Crime' Trial With Prosecutors Blaming Ukrainian 'State Authorities' After four years of speculation, leaks, and briefings by anonymous sources, the world is finally about to hear evidence given publicly under oath in a German courtroom about how the Nord Stream gas pipelines were blown up -- in a case that could prove politically explosive. German prosecutors have identified seven Ukrainian suspects, but just one of them is in the dock in the trial beginning on October 14. He is named as Serhii K. in court documents that say he is suspected of a being an accomplice to a war crime. That classification has caused outrage. But German prosecutors have further raised the stakes by stating the suspects were operating "on behalf of state authorities in Ukraine." Kyiv has always strictly denied any involvement in the attack, which damaged crucial energy infrastructure serving Germany -- one of its most important military backers in its fight since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. Nord Stream is majority-owned by Russia's state-controlled Gazprom and co-financed by major European energy companies. It was constructed to deliver Russian gas directly to Germany, bypassing transit states such as Ukraine and Poland, which had tense relations with Moscow. The suspected sabotage and subsequent gas leaks happened in September 2022, rendering the pipelines as inoperable. Western governments originally accused Russia of carrying out the blasts, but German investigators started forming a case that said a group of Ukrainian divers hired a yacht and planted explosives on the seabed. "At the end of February 2022, he and other military personnel, on behalf of state authorities in Ukraine, developed the plan," says a summary of the indictment released by prosecutors. "The aim was to permanently halt gas deliveries via the pipelines and prevent Russia from using the revenue from the natural gas trade to finance its war efforts." During the trial, the prosecution will have to lay out its evidence for a conspiracy and the full extent of it. "That is the crucial question: How much came from the top of the Ukrainian political system or how much was prepared by some insiders in the intelligence service?" Stefan Meister, a specialist on Russia and Eastern Europe at the German Council on Foreign Relations, told RFE/RL. "The key political question is the role of Zelenskyy and the presidential administration. And there we still have no proof that they were really involved," he added. Kuznetsov's German lawyer, Jes Meyer-Lohkamp, said prosecutors "have provided any direct, evidence of our client's involvement" the German court will have to determine whether Nord Stream The Hanseatic Higher Regional Court in Hamburg has scheduled two hearings every week until at least February, with no specified end date yet. As the case unfolds, it will also feed into bitter disputes in Germany about ongoing support for Ukraine. The main opposition party, Alternative for Germany (AfD), is highly critical of this support and calls for close ties to Russia instead. Evidence of Ukrainian involvement in the Nord Stream attack "would strengthen the AfD's argumentation against this support for Ukraine," said Meister. "They have all these narratives about Ukrainian corruption, a failed state…. It would resonate also in parts of German society." The AfD has recently won key regional elections and is piling the pressure on Chancellor Friedrich Merz's government over Ukraine, immigration, and economic concerns. Merz's response has been to double-down on his current policies, including on Ukraine. Most recently, he was in Kyiv on October 4 with a new aid package including joint production of interceptors to shoot down Russian jet-powered drones. Mikhaylo Honchar, head of the Kyiv-based Strategy XXI Global Studies Center, told RFE/RL this would likely continue regardless of what comes out at the trial. "If you take into consideration real Russian policy, which is directed against the EU and NATO, and Russia's anti-German rhetoric, I think the government of Germany will avoid steps which would undermine the bilateral relationship" with Ukraine, he said. He added that the prosecution case was "absurd," citing German media reports that the attack may have been a Russian false-flag operation. But in any case, Honchar said, a guilty verdict would be met with a clear response in Ukraine. "Many people will say: 'If our guys did it, they are heroes.'"

results.title: Trump faces a new crisis with Kyiv after the agreement on Russian diesel
highlights: Trump faces a new crisis with Kyiv after the agreement on Russian diesel Ukrainians and Europeans receive with bewilderment the decision of the USA to suspend the sanctions on Putin's fuel Trump's new diplomatic crisis over Ukraine erupted on Friday at Steve Witkoff's exclusive golf club, Shell Bay, on the outskirts of Miami. Senior Ukrainian and European officials had traveled there to hold talks with Trump's peace envoys, Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the president's son-in-law. They planned to discuss updated proposals to end the war in Ukraine before a new trip to Russia. But both soon made an announcement that left their interlocutors and much of the world stunned. The Americans communicated that the United States would suspend sanctions on Russian diesel. They also conveyed a firm request from Trump: that Ukraine stop attacking Russian oil refineries. Now the dispute has become the most serious crisis between Washington and Kyiv since the outbreak of tension in the Oval Office with the Ukrainian president last year. The future of US support for Ukraine is once again at stake. The escalation of recriminations has highlighted how Trump's efforts to lower energy prices before next month's midterm legislative elections threaten to destabilize the fragile negotiations over Ukraine. For Ukrainians and their European allies, attacks on Russian refineries are Kyiv's most effective way of responding to Russian bombings against Ukraine's energy grid. Zelensky has stated that he is willing to stop attacking energy infrastructure if Russia does the same. But Russia has refused. Despite this, Trump considers the Ukrainian attacks an offense against an administration that has continued to provide intelligence and some military support to Ukraine, despite the harsh statements by the American president against Zelensky. Diesel prices, in particular, have become a headache for Trump, because they increase the costs for farmers just as the harvest season begins and there are only a few weeks left until the midterm elections. On Sunday, Trump claimed on social media that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" with immediate effect. Neither side confirmed the agreement. "They agreed to it because I said they agreed to it," Trump stated on Monday at the White House. He also reiterated his frustration with Zelensky. "I think Putin is more eager to reach an agreement than Zelensky," said the president. On Monday, European and Ukrainian leaders suggested they would be willing to accept an energy truce, but expressed doubts about whether Russia would respect it. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha noted that Moscow had attacked Ukrainian energy infrastructure on Sunday night, "a few hours after" the announcement. Friday's meeting at Witkoff's golf club lasted about six hours, largely dedicated to exploring what conditions could make future peace negotiations possible. Among the issues discussed were, for example, Ukraine's accession to the European Union and territorial control. But the agreement between Trump and Putin regarding diesel quickly overshadowed the rest of the conversations. On Friday, Zelenskyy described the agreement to allow imports of Russian diesel to lower prices as a "weak decision." As the dispute intensified, Trump stated on Saturday that Ukraine needed "a new president." Several European leaders, including French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, publicly expressed their support for Zelenskyy. Members of the U.S. Congress criticized the diesel deal because, according to them, it helps fund the Russian war machine. "The United States should not provide Putin with a financial lifeline while Russia continues to kill Ukrainian civilians," a bipartisan group of six senators, including Republicans Susan Collins of Maine and John Curtis of Utah, said in a statement on Sunday. "The administration must rectify this immediately." Björn Seibert, a senior EU official who attended Friday's meeting in Florida, briefed the ambassadors of the 27 member states on the meeting on Sunday. The ambassadors were stunned. One of the main conclusions of the meeting in Florida, Seibert explained to them, was that the Americans were maintaining more contacts with the Russians than they were publicly acknowledging. The Trump administration argues that the agreements with Putin, in addition to contributing to lower energy prices, would facilitate an agreement in Ukraine because they would demonstrate to Russia that it can return to the global economy if it agrees to make concessions in the conflict.

results.title: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, prepares for renewed war: report
highlights: Iran fortifies nuclear sites, prepares for renewed war: report Iran is fortifying nuclear sites and threatening wider regional retaliation as it prepares for possible renewed US strikes after November's midterm elections. Iran is strengthening its nuclear and military facilities, mobilising supporters and threatening a wider regional conflict as it prepares for the possibility of renewed war with the United States, according to a report by *The Wall Street Journal.* Iranian leaders believe US President Donald Trump could launch fresh attacks after the 3 November midterm elections, prompting Tehran to reinforce sensitive sites and warn Washington that another offensive would trigger a more devastating response, the newspaper reported on Tuesday. Citing Iranian officials and people familiar with regional communications, the *WSJ* said Tehran had issued both public and private warnings that renewed US strikes could lead to attacks on American interests and Gulf allies. Satellite imagery has shown Iran strengthening defences around nuclear facilities and border areas, while authorities have stepped up pro-government rallies and promoted military training for civilians. Iran's limited ability to counter advanced US fighter jets, high-altitude bombers and cruise missiles has pushed Tehran to rely increasingly on threats of wider retaliation to deter Washington, according to the report. Sanam Vakil, director of the Middle East and North Africa programme at London based Chatham House, said the prospect of war also served Iran's leadership as it grappled with diplomatic, economic and political deadlock. Iranian officials have raised the possibility of launching ground incursions into neighbouring countries in response to further US attacks, according to people familiar with Tehran's warnings. Senior Iranian national security official Mohsen Rezaei warned on Sunday that the United Arab Emirates could be targeted, along with regional data centres and internet cables. Tehran has also warned Arab officials that critical infrastructure, including Saudi oil facilities, could come under attack if fighting resumes, the *WSJ* reported. The threats come as Saudi Arabia faces mounting attacks from Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthi movement. A Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's airport on Saturday killed at least 13 people and wounded hundreds, according to the newspaper, which described it as the deadliest attack on the US or its Gulf allies during the conflict linked to the war with Iran. Iran has also told intermediaries that it could respond more forcefully against American military personnel, including by attempting to sink US warships and inflict casualties among their crews. The warnings highlight the risks to the Gulf's vital economic infrastructure if Trump orders another round of strikes. The US military is also preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities, with a third aircraft carrier strike group and an additional Marine unit heading towards the region according to the outlet. The Pentagon is considering sending more air defence systems and ammunition to American bases across the region. Trump ruled out launching an attack before the midterm elections last week but publicly raised the possibility of striking Iran's Mount Pickaxe nuclear site. US officials said the military was developing several options for renewed strikes. Direct fighting between Washington and Tehran has eased considerably since late July, when Trump backed away from plans for a major escalation, partly over concerns about dwindling interceptor missile stocks needed to protect American and regional targets. The lull has nevertheless allowed both sides to prepare for another confrontation. Iran has used the period to rebuild missile and drone production facilities and replenish its weapons stockpiles, while Washington has intensified economic pressure on Tehran. Meanwhile, attacks on commercial shipping and tankers in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz have increased. At least three merchant vessels came under attack over the weekend, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency. A drone strike on the Emirati tanker Petro Dolphin near Oman on Sunday sparked a fire aboard the vessel and left two Indian sailors missing. **Iran reinforces nuclear sites and mobilises civilians** Satellite images taken by Vantor and analysed by the Washington-based Institute for Science and International Security show Iran constructing new defensive barriers around its Pickaxe Mountain and Natanz nuclear facilities. Behnam Ben Taleblu, senior director of the Iran programme at the Washington-based Foundation for Defense of Democracies, said Tehran's political rhetoric and military preparations indicated it was actively preparing for another confrontation. He described the measures as serving both deterrence and war planning.

results.title: Ukraine Reports No Early Warning Before Russian Missile Strike on Kyiv Amid U.S. Pressure Over Energy Ceasefire- The Defense News
highlights: KYIV, — Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Tuesday that Ukraine received no advance warning from Western partners before a Russian ballistic missile attack struck Kyiv overnight, raising concerns about intelligence sharing amid reported U.S. pressure on Ukraine to stop attacking Russian oil refineries. Preliminary reports indicated that Russia fired five or possibly six ballistic missiles, identified in some accounts as Iskander-M or S-400 types, reportedly from the Bryansk region. The Ukrainian Air Force said it had not received advance surveillance information about the launches and detected the targets during the attack. The cause of the missed warning remains under investigation. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said at the Warsaw Security Forum that military intelligence sharing with the United States remained intact, attributing the delayed warning to the specific weapons used. Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat has acknowledged that intelligence from partners does not always arrive and that technical problems have occurred previously. The wider Russian assault involved more than 100 weapons, including jet-powered drones, loitering munitions and ballistic missiles. In Kharkiv, a strike destroyed a residential apartment building, killing four people and injuring 41, according to Zelenskyy. The Russian Defence Ministry said its forces targeted Ukrainian military-industrial facilities, logistics centres, railway and port infrastructure, and vessels allegedly carrying military cargo. Ukrainian authorities continued assessing damage and responding to the attacks. The incident comes amid reports that Washington has threatened to restrict intelligence sharing and weapons support unless Ukraine stops attacking Russian energy infrastructure. Ukraine relies significantly on U.S. missile-launch detection capabilities, including the Space-Based Infrared System (SBIRS). Missile expert Fabian Hoffmann has noted that European allies have limited ability to replace these capabilities. On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump announced an proposed energy ceasefire under which Russia and Ukraine would stop attacking each other's energy infrastructure. Zelenskyy initially said the announcement was news to him but confirmed on Tuesday that Ukraine had not struck Russian oil refineries or energy sites during the two days following the announcement. Ukraine reported that Russia struck six Ukrainian energy facilities on Monday but did not target energy infrastructure during the overnight period leading into Tuesday. The latest attacks instead focused on transport and logistics. The Kremlin has not officially confirmed the agreement. Spokesman Dmitry Peskov said contacts on the matter were continuing, while Russia's Defence Ministry denied Ukrainian allegations of attacks on energy facilities in recent strikes. Trump has blamed Ukrainian refinery attacks for contributing to rising U.S. fuel prices, although market analysts have identified the U.S.-led war in Iran as a major factor. Reports have also described an arrangement involving Russian diesel imports to the United States following Trump's discussions with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday; its precise terms and status remain unclear. Zelenskyy called for reciprocal de-escalation and urged Ukraine's partners to pressure Russia to stop attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure. Although Ukraine has paused attacks on Russian energy facilities, it continues targeting other sites inside Russia with long-range drones. Russia's Defence Ministry reported shooting down 604 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the Sea of Azov overnight. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 417 drones targeted the Moscow region, with 65 intercepted near the capital. In the Kaluga region, attacks damaged a school, two houses and a vehicle. Sybiha argued that Washington's reported request to halt Ukrainian refinery attacks demonstrated Kyiv's increased leverage. Referring to an Oval Office meeting last year when Trump told Zelenskyy that he did not have the cards, Sybiha said: “In less than two years, we have gone from ‘having no cards’ to ‘not playing your cards’.” Ukraine's investigation into the missed missile warning continues as questions remain over the proposed energy ceasefire, Russia's attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure and the reliability of advance intelligence for future missile strikes.

results.title: Zelensky: Ukraine received no intelligence about Russia missile attack
highlights: KYIV, Ukraine (AP) — Ukraine received no early warning from its partners about five Russian ballistic missiles that hit civilian infrastructure in the capital of Kyiv, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Tuesday, as tensions rise between the Ukrainian leader and President Donald Trump. Zelenskyy did not specify which partners he was talking about. He characterized the barrage as “particularly vile” and emphasized that receiving intelligence from partners about such attacks “helps save lives” and is “one of the most critical issues.” Trump said the U.S. has not stopped sharing intelligence with Ukraine. “We are helping them, and we are sharing intel,” Trump told reporters at the White House. “We want the war to end, so we’re working with them and with Russia on getting the war to end.” Zelenskyy’s remarks come days after Trump unleashed biting criticism of him, including comments that i t was time for a new president in Ukraine and that Zelenskyy has not done enough to end the war. The criticism marks perhaps the lowest point in their relationship since their disastrous Oval Office meeting in February 2025. Kyiv continues to rely heavily on Washington for military assistance, including U.S.-made Patriot missile-defense systems and intelligence. The U.S. has the capability to immediately spot Russian ballistic missile launches. American officials have in the past notified Ukraine about launches to allow it to issue missile warnings to the public and to use air defenses against incoming missiles. Asked whether Ukraine received an explanation for the lack of intelligence ahead of the overnight missile strikes, a senior Ukrainian official said it was described as a “failure,” suggesting it was the result of circumstances such as weather conditions rather than a deliberate decision. The official spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to give an official statement on the matter. Russia’s war in Ukraine has not seen major shifts on the ground since last year, but Ukraine is struggling to fend off Moscow’s intensified aerial attacks that include speedy ballistic missiles and high-flying jet-powered drones. Downing the missiles has been a challenge because of a shortage of Patriot missiles caused by the U.S.-led war in Iran. Russia’s Iskander short-range ballistic missiles take just a few minutes to reach targets in Ukraine. Zelenskyy said Russia had attacked Ukraine with more than 100 weapons since Monday evening. A residential building in the northeastern city of Kharkiv was destroyed, killing four people despite an all-night rescue operation, he said. Russia has increasingly used attacks on civilian infrastructure such as energy facilities to deny Ukrainians power, heat and running water during the 4½-year war, hoping to wear down public support for Ukraine’s response to Moscow’s full-scale invasion. Trump has blamed Ukraine’s earlier strikes on Russian oil refineries for record U.S. diesel prices — rather than the war in Iran. He struck a deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Friday to import diesel from Russia in an attempt to bring fuel prices down ahead of U.S. midterm elections. Meanwhile, Trump claimed Sunday that Russia and Ukraine had agreed on an “energy ceasefire” in which both parties would refrain from striking each other’s energy infrastructure. Russia has not confirmed the existence of such a deal. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said only that “contacts on this matter continue.” Zelenskyy on Tuesday said Ukraine had not struck Russian oil refineries or other energy sites in the two days since Trump announced the purported deal. He criticized Moscow for what he said were Russian attacks on Ukrainian energy facilities and infrastructure in the time since Trump’s announcement. “These are absolutely clear signals that they have no intention of refraining from strikes on Ukraine,” Zelenskyy said. The claim that Ukraine has halted its strikes on energy sites could not be independently verified, but neither Russian officials nor media have reported Ukrainian attacks on oil refineries since the energy truce was announced. Strikes on Kharkiv kill 4 and wound 41 Russian strikes across Ukraine caused injuries and deaths overnight Monday and into Tuesday. In addition to the four deaths in the apartment building in Kharkiv, 41 people were wounded in the city in one evening alone, Zelenskyy said. a Russian strike in Kyiv’s Darnytskyi district, the Kyiv city military administration said. A Russian drone hit a residential building in the village of Murovane, near the western city of Lviv, during a morning attack Tuesday, Lviv Mayor Andrii Sadovyi said. killed in the Fastiv district of the Kyiv region, two others were hurt in a Russian attack on the area, said Tymur Tkachenko, head of the regional military administration. A Russian drone struck an educational institution in the center of Rivne in northwest Ukraine, wounding 14 people, according to Oleksandr Koval, head of the Rivne regional military administration. The Russian Defense Ministry said in a statement Tuesday that its forces launched strikes “against Ukrainian military-industrial facilities, logistics centers, railway and port infrastructure, as well as vessels involved in delivering military cargo to Ukraine.” The ministry also said a bulk carrier headed to the port of Mykolaiv with military cargo on board was hit in the estuary of the Bug River along the Black Sea. The Russian Defense Ministry on Tuesday said its air defenses overnight shot down 604 Ukrainian drones over Russian regions and the Sea of Azov. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said 417 drones targeted the Moscow region. Most were downed far away, while 65 were intercepted as they approached the Russian capital. A school, two private houses and a car were damaged in the attack in the Kaluga region southwest of Moscow, Gov. Vladislav Shapsha said.
